Title: Retirement: SQL Data Sync will be retired on September 30th, 2027

Body.Content:
SQL Data Sync will be retired on September 30th, 2027. By the date, please consider migrating to alternatives data replication/synchronization solutions. 

We encourage you to consider alternative solutions prior to the retirement date, so you can complete your migration on time. The right solution depends on your individual use case, with services like Azure Data Factory, Azure Functions, read replicas or SQL features like linked server, mirroring, Always-On, and transaction replication as alternatives.  

From now to September 30th, 2027, you can continue to use SQL Data Sync without disruption. On September 30th, 2027—workloads running SQL Data Sync will be deleted and associated application data will be lost.

Additional communications will follow as the retirement date approaches.

Required action

To avoid service disruptions, please follow our instructions here to migrate to replacement options by September 30th, 2027.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A.
Azure SQL Database - Microsoft Q&A

If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request. 

  1. For Issue type, select Technical.  
  2. For Subscription, select your subscription. 
  3. For Service, select My services, then select SQL Database. 
  4. Select the Azure resource that you are creating a support request for.  
  5. For Summary, type a description of your issue.    
  6. For Problem type, select Data Sync, Replication, CDC and Change Tracking.    
  7. For Problem subtype, select SQL Data Sync. 

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.
